content:
extending: How to extend furb: a def in a word, which lives as long as its chain, and an extension, which a host enables on each chain of a life.
frontend-design: Guidance for distinctive, intentional visual design when building new UI or reshaping an existing one. Helps with aesthetic direction, typography, and making choices that don't read as templated defaults.
graphify: any input (code, docs, papers, images) - knowledge graph - clustered communities - HTML + JSON + audit report
grill: Automated agentic workflow that drives a software request through interview → plan → audit/fix → implement/verify → end-to-end test, asking the user only at design-decision boundaries. The implement/verify/test cycle is fully autonomous — the verifier loops back to the implementer until acceptance criteria pass, the orchestrator commits on verify pass, and only then does the slow phase-4 test run. Use when the user types `/grill <ask>` or asks for "automated grill loop". Each agent runs in a freshly composed single-turn `claude -p` subprocess (with `--effort max`) to eliminate context drift.
grill-me: Interview the user relentlessly about a plan or design until reaching shared understanding, resolving each branch of the decision tree. Use when user wants to stress-test a plan, get grilled on their design, or mentions "grill me".
pr-monitor: Monitor GitHub PRs for CI failures and review comments, auto-fix issues, and reply in-thread. Use this skill whenever the user says "monitor PR", "watch PR", "start a monitor", "keep an eye on #N", or wants autonomous PR lifecycle management until merge. Supports monitoring multiple PRs in parallel as background agents. Also triggers when the user says "restart monitor" or "resume monitoring".
web-design-guidelines: Review UI code for Web Interface Guidelines compliance. Use when asked to "review my UI", "check accessibility", "audit design", "review UX", or "check my site against best practices".
webapp-testing: Toolkit for interacting with and testing local web applications using Playwright. Supports verifying frontend functionality, debugging UI behavior, capturing browser screenshots, and viewing browser logs.

write(Text("notes.md", "one\ntwo\n"))
notes = read("notes.md")
said = await bash("echo hi")
await wait(0.01)
helper = chain("helper")
got = await prompt(int, "Give 2.", on=helper)
close(got + len(notes.lines) + int(clock() > 0) + int(0 <= chance() < 1))
